content.user_title: Build Reliable Service Workers and Offline PWAs
content.value_statement: Service workers can leave users with stale pages, broken updates, or unsafe offline caches. This skill guides lifecycle handling, cache ownership, offline fallbacks, and browser-aware PWA behavior.
actual_capabilities: Guides worker registration, installation, activation, waiting states, and scope selection.
Shows app-prefixed, versioned cache cleanup that preserves other applications' caches.
Matches cache-first, network-first, and stale-while-revalidate strategies to content types.
Provides a GET navigation handler with a precached offline page and a 503 fallback.
Explains bounded background retries, idempotency keys, and user-visible update flows.
Covers manifest fields, browser feature detection, private-data exclusions, and Workbox adoption.
limitations: Contains guidance and small JavaScript examples, not a complete application or automated test suite.
Background Sync and installation prompts have browser-dependent support.
HTTP and CDN header policy alone is outside this skill's focus.
Account-aware offline storage and push behavior require application-specific implementation beyond the included examples.

use_cases.title: Plan controlled PWA updates

use_cases.title: Review offline and browser behavior

prompt_templates.title: Explain the worker lifecycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain registration, installation, activation, and waiting states for my first service worker. Describe when skipWaiting and clients.claim are appropriate.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: understand lifecycle behavior before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Add offline navigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a service worker to my application with app-prefixed versioned caches and a precached offline page. Preserve other applications' caches.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: implement a basic offline navigation path.

prompt_templates.title: Review caching and update behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my worker for stale HTML, private-data caching, cache ownership, and update handling. Recommend content-specific strategies and a user-visible update flow.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: improve an existing service worker.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Workbox offline workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Workbox routing and background retries for my PWA. Include idempotency keys, bounded retries, account isolation, logout cleanup, and unsupported-browser fallbacks.

output_examples.input: Plan offline navigation for a small web application.
output: Register the worker at the intended application scope.
Precache the offline page in a versioned, app-prefixed cache.
Try the network for GET navigations and return the offline page when the request fails.
Delete only obsolete caches owned by this application during activation.

output_examples.input: Review a PWA that shows old pages after deployment.
output: Check whether the new worker is waiting for existing tabs to close.
Use network-first or stale-while-revalidate for documents instead of indefinite cache-first behavior.
Show a refresh prompt when the new worker is ready.
Test activation and navigation with multiple tabs and a slow network.

output_examples.input: Plan background retries for failed writes.
output: Queue only eligible failed writes in IndexedDB.
Use idempotency keys and bounded retries to prevent duplicate operations.
Expose a clear failure state and a foreground retry path.
Feature-detect Background Sync and provide a fallback where it is unavailable.

best_practices: Namespace and version caches, then delete only obsolete caches owned by your application.
Exclude private responses unless offline storage includes account partitioning and logout cleanup.
Test offline navigation, slow networks, and user-visible updates in supported browsers.
anti_patterns: Delete every cache on the origin during worker activation.
Cache mutation responses or private data without explicit safeguards.
Serve stale HTML indefinitely or activate updates without considering existing sessions.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does this skill include a complete PWA?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and small examples that must be adapted to your application.

faq.question: Should I use Workbox?
faq.answer: The skill recommends Workbox for non-trivial applications because it provides routing, caching strategies, revision-based precaching, and cleanup.

faq.question: Does Cache Storage respect no-store automatically?
faq.answer: No. Explicitly exclude private responses unless your offline design handles account partitioning and logout cleanup.

faq.question: Does Background Sync work in every browser?
faq.answer: No. Feature-detect support and provide foreground retries; Periodic Background Sync has limited support.

faq.question: Is a service worker always required for PWA installation?
faq.answer: No. Installation criteria vary by browser, and beforeinstallprompt is not universal. Use HTTPS, a suitable manifest, and platform-specific fallbacks.
